Progressive motor-neuron degeneration; denervation muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79% or more. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness, not intrinsic lung damage.
Primary phalangeal osteolysis and sclerosis; associated redness and swelling do not establish separate skin disease.

Inherited juvenile open-angle glaucoma affecting the eye and optic nerve.
Inherited blistering skin disorder; intellectual disability/microcephaly and corneal opacity each occur in 30-79%. Pneumonia is a separate infection.
Compensatory overexpansion of pulmonary tissue.
Metabolic urea-cycle defect with hepatic dysfunction; encephalopathy characterizes adult type II but is not established as common across the umbrella.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with brain atrophy and regression; optic atrophy is occasional, 5-29%.
Diffuse hyperfunctioning thyroid enlargement, predominantly autoimmune Graves disease; clinically significant orbitopathy is not consistently >=30%.
X-linked intellectual disability; high myopia and blepharophimosis each affect 2/8 patients, below 30%.
Malignant smooth muscle tumour arising in the heart; the broad EBV-related ancestor does not establish infection in this concept.
Skin, hair, nail and dental dysplasia define the disease; eyelid abnormalities and ptosis occur in 30-79%.
